payload.name: Resolve relative dates and preserve first-time markers in event extraction
payload.description: When extracting event memories, if the source message uses a relative time (yesterday, last week, today) or a first/ordinal marker, resolve the exact date from the message/session timestamp and keep the marker in the candidate content.
content: Scan each source message for relative time expressions ('yesterday', 'last week', 'today') and resolve them to concrete dates using the message/session timestamp; store the resolved date instead of vague phrasing like 'recently'.
If the message includes a first-time or ordinal marker ('for the first time', 'first', 'once'), preserve that qualifier in the extracted event content because it is a durable, queryable fact.

solves: Extraction often loses explicit event facts by paraphrasing relative dates as vague terms (e.g., 'recently') and dropping 'first time' qualifiers, making later date or ordinal questions unanswerable. This rule applies whenever a message describes an event relative to its timestamp or marks an occurrence as first, and instructs extraction to resolve and preserve those details.
